title: Animation and art donor catalog
bodyMarkdown: # Animation and art donor catalog Source specification 2.1 research · Verified 2026-09-08 · **Adopted intake reference; implementation active, with current inventory/proof in19/26.** This is a curated intake queue for chapter 21's inhabited nonlinear world, not permission to download everything or a claim that the packs already fit. Creator pages, explicit free-file lists and licence statements were inspected. Four creator preview images/GIFs were viewed in an isolated browser. No asset archive, font or source sheet was downloaded, installed, edited, rehosted or added to the public site. Native archive completeness, dimensions, pivots, frame timing and runtime appearance remain unverified until intake after go. Paid additions are excluded. The existing LuizMelo Martial Hero remains the player. Its inspected local manifest uses 200×200 frame cells, a foot pivot at(100,122), approximately 52 px visible idle height and a 22×46 collision guide. The transparent cell is not the body's scale. Compare donors beside that actual actor at native size before choosing world scale; a 32 px NPC and a 250 px sheet cell do not become compatible merely because both are pixel art. The character's authored frames stay coherent; never regenerate isolated poses to manufacture a sprite sheet. ## First intake order 1. **Boss:** Evil Wizard 2 first, with Evil Wizard 3 as the closer human-scale alternative. Keep only the one whose actual swing/contact/death reads best in the arena. Fire Knight is a stronger alternate moveset if its proportions and credit requirement work. 2. **Sparse enemies:** Monsters Creatures Fantasy 2 rat/bat or one original-pack creature. Choose one ground and one air silhouette at most for the first connected route; a four-creature archive is not a demand to use all four. 3. **Residents:** Gothicvania Town's side-view townsfolk first. The free Blacksmith is an excellent service-motion reference but a conditional actor because its32px proportions are squat. The49-NPC pack supplies idle personalities, not a finished walking/service cast. 4. **Environment and detail:** retain the original dex.place architecture. Test selective Magic Cliffs depth and one small fire/water detail; do not replace the world with a donor demo. 5. **UI:** compare one Kenney frame family with m5x7 or Monogram for short labels. Keep Daniel for `dex`, and the readable body/financial-text system for articles, accounts and banking. All placements, palette adaptation and animation timings below are proposed production choices. The art/use restrictions in 01/03/21 remain unchanged; none of Dex's illustrations is a donor or generation reference. ## A. Combat cast | ID / source | Verified free content and licence | Proposed role / fit / adaptation | |---|---|---| | AD-01 · [Evil Wizard 2 — LuizMelo](https://luizmelo.itch.io/evil-wizard-2) | Name-your-price free ZIP. Idle8, run8, two attacks8 each, jump2, fall2, hit3, death7. Creator explicitly permits commercial use under **CC0**; credit appreciated. | **Primary boss candidate.** Tall staff, robe mass and distinct purple effect make readable anticipation possible. Same artist as the hero supports comparison but proves neither matching scale nor frame registration. The inspected GIF has generous transparent margins: derive body/collision separately. Preserve complete attack and death before the black-to-product-menu transition. | | AD-02 · [Evil Wizard 3 — LuizMelo](https://luizmelo.itch.io/evil-wizard-3) | Free ZIP; stated33×53px character. Idle10, walk8, run8, jump/fall3 each, attack13, hit3, death18. **CC0**, commercial use allowed. | **Reserve boss or non-hostile attendant silhouette.** Its stated body height is close to Martial Hero's visible 52 px. A 53 px actor should not be enlarged into a giant to compensate for weak arena composition. Long death sequence needs an authored hold/transition, not a fabricated loop. | | AD-03 · [Monsters Creatures Fantasy — LuizMelo](https://luizmelo.itch.io/monsters-creatures-fantasy) | Free base archive plus separately listed1.2/1.3 archives. **CC0**. Skeleton idle/walk4, attack8, shield/hit/death4; mushroom and goblin idle4/run8/attack8/hit4/death4; flying eye flight8/attack8/hit4/death4. | **Primary small-creature alternative.** Skeleton supplies an explicit block pose; eye supplies aerial motion. Verify which listed archive carries which base/update frames rather than importing only an attack update. Collision, knockback and health remain game-owned; a hit sheet does not prove contact logic. Avoid filling each room with the whole set. | | AD-04 · [Monsters Creatures Fantasy 2 — LuizMelo](https://luizmelo.itch.io/monsters-creatures-fantasy-2) | Free/name-your-price, **CC0**. Rat40×20 with idle10/run8/bite12/hurt3/death6; slime44×18 with idle14/walk6/attack19/hurt3/death11; bat51×38 with fly/attack11, hurt3 and fall/death stages. Mimic42×30 includes opening, transform, walking, two attacks and death. | **First ground/air test pair: rat and bat.** Small bodies suit sparse reservoir encounters. Mimic is reserve: do not turn donation boxes, archive doors or ordinary files into misleading hostile objects. Distinguish flight bounds, hurtboxes and fall/death landing from the transparent cell. | | AD-05 · [Fire Worm — LuizMelo](https://luizmelo.itch.io/fire-worm) | Free `Fire Worm.zip`; **CC0**. Stated51×41 body with idle/walk9, attack16, hit3, death8. Separate19×11 fireball lists movement and explosion. | **Reserve hazard-creature.** Useful separate projectile anatomy and ground-attached attack. Bright fire and a chunky body could make a quiet passage too busy. Use only in an authored pocket, keep projectile/source state independently timed, and exclude permanent looping attacks in service areas. | | AD-06 · [Elementals: Fire Knight — chierit](https://chierit.itch.io/elementals-fire-knight) | `Elementals_fire_knight_FREE_v1.1.zip` includes12 human-form animations: idle/run/jump/air attack/roll, three attacks, special attack, defend/hit/death. **CC BY 4.0**; credit chierit and note modifications. Aseprite source is advertised. Thirteen Elemental Mode extras are in the paid FULL archive, not free. The page additionally asks not to resell assets. | **Reserve sword-boss candidate.** Inspected free attack preview has a substantial blade and clear side-view body; this is a moveset prospect, not a new protagonist. Use only the free human set, no paid transformation/fireball dependency. Check actual attack reach and body height against the hero; retain subdued world palette and readable contact. | | AD-07 · [Bringer of Death — Clembod](https://clembod.itch.io/bringer-of-death-free) | Free ZIP. Idle/walk8, attack10, hurt3, death10, cast9 and separate spell16. **Custom terms:** personal/commercial use and modification allowed; redistribution/resale prohibited. Not CC0 or CC BY. | **Conditional reserve.** Robed melee/caster guardian has useful complete action categories. The broad redistribution wording requires exact downloaded licence/deployment review before public web embedding. Never put the donor archive or sprites in the website's downloadable documentation bundle. Prefer the CC0 choices if that deployment boundary is unresolved. | ## B. Residents and usable environment material | ID / source | Verified free content and licence | Proposed role / fit / adaptation | |---|---|---| | AD-08 · [Gothicvania Town — Ansimuz](https://ansimuz.itch.io/gothicvania-town) | Free `GothicVania-town-files.zip`: two-layer parallax, tiles, houses/barrels/props, four NPCs with idle+walk and a Phaser demo. Page lists **CC0**. `GothicVania-Town-Plus_Files.zip` requires payment; recent Plus towers/blacksmith/stables are not assumed free. | **Primary resident intake.** Viewed base scene shows natural side-view townsfolk rather than top-down miniatures, and useful doorstep/prop scale. Select one or two actors for counter/refuge; adjust scene lighting around their pixels. No claimed greeting/work animation in this base pack. Do not import the medieval street composition, demo code, music or fonts wholesale; inventory each component's rights separately. | | AD-09 · [Free Lively NPC: Blacksmith — chierit](https://chierit.itch.io/free-lively-npc-blacksmith) | Free 87 kB archive; **CC BY 4.0**. 32×32 sprites at recommended 6 fps. Two bored loops10 frames each, greeting4, idle4, work loops5/6. | **Service-animation reserve.** The viewed work preview shows a compact craftsman gesturing around a tool/waist-height station. Excellent candidate for meaningful acknowledgment and work pauses; it is visibly squat compared with Martial Hero. Do not upscale to 52 px and quietly double its pixel pitch. Test a recessed counter placement, otherwise use it as motion reference and choose a better-proportioned resident. | | AD-10 · [Free Lively NPCs — chierit](https://chierit.itch.io/lively-npcs) | Free `Lively_NPCs_v3.1.zip`,49 sprites at 32×32; **idle-only**, 4–6 frames, recommended 6 fps. **CC BY 4.0**. The separate 48×48 Victorian Steampunk pack is paid and not included. | **Background-stationary reserve.** Useful single sheltered resident, not 49 new required inhabitants. Author's larger paid figures and free ones have different scale; avoid mixing casually. No verified walk, greeting, sitting, handover or four-direction set here. Stillness should remain, rather than every character bouncing in a synchronized loop. | | AD-11 · [Magic Cliffs — Ansimuz](https://ansimuz.itch.io/magic-cliffs-environment) | Free MagicCliffsGodot/Gamekit archives; parallax background, tiles and props, a player moveset and two named enemies. Page lists **CC0**. `Magic Cliffs Addon.zip` is paid: extra foliage and additional player/enemy clips are excluded. | **Reservoir/lookout depth reserve.** Select rock silhouettes, sea-distance layers or ledge material to bridge quiet exterior compositions. Do not replace the current hero or imply new player abilities from its included clips. Animated water frames are not established by the page's ocean-view tag. Bundled music/project files get separate intake; SunoB remains the theme. | | AD-12 · [Industrial Parallax Background — Ansimuz](https://ansimuz.itch.io/industrial-parallax-background) | Free layered, seamless industrial-night background and PSD; looped music is advertised. **Licence discrepancy:** prose says no attribution needed, while asset metadata names **CC BY 4.0**. | **Conditional far-depth reserve.** Use restrained distant gantry/machinery silhouettes behind the original arena or Dispatch. Preserve depth falloff; no baked-perspective donor foreground. Credit conservatively under CC BY 4.0 and inspect the actual archive licence before export. Do not call thisCC0, and do not reuse its music without verifying the specific track rights. | ## C. Small motion, UI and typography | ID / source | Verified free content and licence | Proposed role / fit / adaptation | |---|---|---| | AD-13 · [Animated Fires — Stealthix](https://stealthix.itch.io/animated-fires) | Free `Fires.zip` and `Fires-Black.zip`; three fire animations with color variants, using Endesga32. **CC0**. Exact grid/frame counts are not stated here. | **First refuge fire test.** A small hearth flame can support the cozy counter without making the whole scene energetic. Separate the luminous source, static housing and world light. Compare at native grid size; use one restrained treatment. Color alternatives are not additional independent art roles. | | AD-14 · [PVFX Foundry — nerijs](https://nerijs.itch.io/pvfx-foundry) | Free 0.6.0 pack, **CC0** rendered sheets/metadata. 34 effects, 96×96 at 20 fps, fixed-grid and packed variants with advertised pivots/timing. Includes Splash Crown, Shoreline Foam, Dripping Runoff and Landing Dust. Creator discloses AI-assisted code/text and deterministic procedural VFX, not generative image output. | **Conditional water/contact reserve.** Test one foam/drip/dust effect only; do not import its unrelated magic catalogue. Reproducibility/pivot claims are creator claims until the archive is inspected. Procedural origin is acceptable to evaluate, but no assumption of hand-authored frames or automatic visual cohesion. Fixed 96 px cells do not determine screen size. | | AD-15 · [Animated Flags — Screaming Brain Studios](https://screamingbrainstudios.itch.io/animated-flags-pack) | Free flat/shaded/individual archives. **CC0**. 229 country designs in shaded/unshaded forms, 16-frame orthographic loops, plus shading sheet; teal rather than transparent backgrounds. | **Cloth-motion reserve, not map-release animation.** Use a plain recolored derivative of an unshaded loop only after keying and edge/grid inspection. Do not add national flags or language selectors merely because they are in the archive. Wind waving is not cutting, falling, unfurling or settling; the map still needs its own independently attached parts and authored state sequence. | | AD-16 · [UI Pack: Pixel Adventure — Kenney](https://kenney.nl/assets/ui-pack-pixel-adventure), with [Input Prompts Pixel](https://kenney.nl/assets/input-prompts-pixel) as its optional control-symbol companion | Both individually free, **CC0**; paid All-in-1 bundle unnecessary. UI pack lists 500 button/panel/slider-related files. Input pack lists 800 16×16 keyboard/mouse/touch/controller glyphs. No authored UI animation is promised. | **Primary UI material study.** Select one compatible border/backing/pressed family; register corners/edges for scale instead of stretching chunky pixels. Supply animations as independently owned UI states, and all text/focus/hit targets as DOM. Only ship supported keyboard/mouse/touch symbols; a gamepad icon does not authorize gamepad scope. | | AD-17 · [m5x7 — Daniel Linssen](https://managore.itch.io/m5x7) | Free TTF, **CC0**. Upper/lowercase, many accented characters, numbers/common symbols. Creator recommends 16 px size and multiples; average width 5, ascender 7, descender 2. | **Primary short-label comparison.** Compact `Inspect`, `Map`, room labels and heading accents. This Daniel is not Daniel Midgley, whose separate font owns the `dex` wordmark. Do not replace readable paragraphs/bank facts; verify actual Vietnamese characters, ₫, punctuation, zoom and fallback before any account UI use. “Many accents” is not complete language coverage. | | AD-18 · [Monogram — datagoblin](https://datagoblin.itch.io/monogram) | Free **CC0** monospace font in TrueType, bitmap and PICO-8 forms; extended and italic TTFs are listed free. The paid $5 thank-you gift is separate; creator explicitly confirms required font files are free. | **Alternate label font.** Test it against m5x7 at equal perceived size and identical labels, not as a second simultaneous UI theme. Extended TTF and small bitmap have different character coverage; do not assume bitmap contains every accent. Preserve readable system/body fallback, actual monetary characters and Daniel branding. | ## Creator preview links actually inspected These URLs were observed in the creator's page HTML or image links, not guessed or reconstructed. They are external preview references only: no local copies, rehosting, tracing from compressed GIFs or extraction of paid frames. An animated browser preview was rendered and inspected at sampled moments; this is not a frame-by-frame timing, licence-archive or contact/pivot acceptance test. | Preview | Exact observed URL | Observation | |---|---|---| | Evil Wizard 2 creator GIF | [View GIF](https://img.itch.zone/aW1hZ2UvNzMyODA0LzQxMzUxODIuZ2lm/original/tc%2FXFz.gif) | 750×750 presentation; substantial margin around the robed figure and large staff effect. The effect/body need separate collision interpretation. | | Free Blacksmith work01 | [View GIF](https://img.itch.zone/aW1nLzUwMDg0MzYuZ2lm/original/xBP8Uz.gif) | 96×96 presentation of the 32 px character; useful small work gesture, visibly compact proportions. | | Fire Knight free first attack | [View GIF](https://img.itch.zone/aW1nLzcwMzM3NDMuZ2lm/original/jTpkYv.gif) | 864×384 showcase; strong side-facing sword pose and readable red/brown silhouette. Preview extent is not source cell/body size. | | Gothicvania base scene | [View PNG](https://img.itch.zone/aW1hZ2UvMTc2NzYzLzgyNTI2Ni5wbmc=/original/Pvg5pE.png) | 800×469 preview with four side-view townsfolk, doors and shared ground line. Warm medieval scenery is reference for resident fit, not the new site's entire aesthetic. | The web fetcher could not render several GIFs, so the originals were viewed through an isolated headless browser instead. The research browser closed afterward. No creator account, download gate, payment or upload was used. ## Reserves rejected from the primary intake - **[Stealthix Animated Effects](https://stealthix.itch.io/animated-effects):** currently $3, custom royalty-free terms and no standalone redistribution; it is not the free CC0 Animated Fires pack. Do not infer free access from shared artwork or creator. - **[Foozle/Pixel Carvel Scallywag Fort](https://foozlecc.itch.io/scallywag-fort):** genuinely free CC0, source `.ase` and animated cannons/flags, but explicitly top-down. Reject its walls/doors as a direct structural kit for this side-view world; no cannon feature follows from its availability. - **[CreativeKind Necromancer Free](https://creativekind.itch.io/necromancer-free):** free custom-commercial-use sprite with idle/run, three attacks, hurt and death; standalone redistribution prohibited. Its third attack references a separate spell pack and source-grid compatibility remains unverified. Retain as a conditional alternate from 21, behind the clearerCC0 boss choices. - **[Kenney Platformer Kit](https://kenney.nl/assets/platformer-kit):** free CC0 but 3D; not a replacement for fully2D world assets. Likewise, mixed top-down packs and commercial game sprite rips are excluded irrespective of visual appeal. - Gothicvania Plus, Magic Cliffs Addon, Fire Knight Elemental Mode and optional font gifts are not included in the free intake. Do not use storefront GIFs to bypass their paid tiers. ## Gaps the catalog does not pretend to solve No inspected free pack here proves a complete side-view archive door with handle/latch/open/close frames, a cable-cut/falling/settled map, or a resident handing over an account service object at the current world's exact scale. Those remain authored asset/state work after go. Existing dex.place mechanism parts can supply aligned structure; this catalogue supplies compatible actors/material/motion leads, not ready-made game behavior. Doors must preserve fixed pivots, entrance/readiness/collision and return anchors. Map wind/cloth loops cannot replace its one-time cut and persistent open state. Water motion is covered only as a conditional splash/foam/drip source and existing calm world-water material; no ocean-view page is treated as proof of animated water. Hearth work/greeting is covered by a small service donor, but a natural-height side-view attendant may still need an authored gesture adaptation. Record these missing roles in 19 rather than marking them acquired because a similarly named pack exists. ## Mandatory intake and scene test after go 1. Acquire only the chosen free archive from its creator. Preserve its exact original, version/date, file hash and included licence; compare free/paid filenames against this dated page evidence. Fonts, audio, demo code and third-party credits remain separate components. 2. Enumerate every clip and frame; record actual cell dimensions, opaque bounds, foot baseline, pivot, loop/hold behavior and required external props/projectiles. Check all stated actions are really present across any update archives. Page counts are discovery evidence, not importer truth. 3. Build one native-size lineup beside the untouched Martial Hero, P02 terminal and current platform. Compare body proportion, pixel pitch, palette, facing and side-view perspective at desktop and phone camera sizes. Reject a weak donor instead of stretching it until the nominal height matches. 4. Exercise complete animations: idle→walk→stop, greeting/work→service panel→return, anticipation→blade/projectile contact→follow-through, hit interruption and full death→black→product menu. Wire collision events independently of animation render rate. No compressed preview GIF becomes the source sheet. 5. Inspect fixed mounts versus moving pieces for fire/door/cloth/map/lift. Match light direction and source size; preserve transparent edges. Use Low/reduced modes without eliminating useful states, and avoid converting every calm room into an effects reel. 6. Test UI9-slicing, native glyph rendering, hover/focus/pressed/disabled/open/close and every long/Vietnamese/account/bank string. Select one pixel heading/label family; body text, accessible names and QR remain ordinary readable DOM. 7. Record licensing/attribution in the private asset register and future reviewed credits. [CC0](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) permits reuse/adaptation without attribution requirement; [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) requires appropriate credit, licence link and indication of changes. Custom restrictions are not interchangeable with either. Preserve the final project attribution even when credit is optional; it is factual documentation, not promotional copy. 8. Publish only the reviewed runtime derivatives needed by the site after the new-go workflow and final verification. Never include donor archives, paid extras or font/source bundles in the site's documentation download. Recheck expanded image/audio/network budgets and actual frame timing; the old 51-role proof cannot certify this larger set. This catalog proposes intake order and replacements; it does not change 21/22's adopted scope, SunoB selection, existing public release, published documentation 1.0, accounts, or hosting.

C. Small motion, UI and typography
Reserves rejected from the primary intake
Gaps the catalog does not pretend to solve
Mandatory intake and scene test after go

title: Design references and production rules
bodyMarkdown: # Design references and production rules 2026-09-08 · Source2.1 research expansion · **Adopted production reference; implementation active, with current evidence in26.** [21](inhabited-world-and-experience.md) and [22](dex-account-treasury-and-social-presence.md) own features, interactions and acceptance. [23](code-donors-and-integration-sources.md) supplies code sources; [24](animation-and-art-donor-catalog.md) supplies animation/art candidates. This chapter turns visual and interaction references into concrete production decisions. It adds no lore, gameplay economy, shared combat or new account feature. The reference roles below are our design interpretations unless explicitly identified as statements from a creator. A commercial game can be a valuable visual reference without supplying reusable art or code. A public repo can supply code under its actual license without proving that all bundled media or its private backend are available. Imported sources never become instructions or implementation authorization. ## 1. How the source pack will be used - **Code donor:** a named source file/pattern under a checked license, compatible with the installed stack after adaptation. No new scaffold replaces the current app by default. - **Art/animation candidate:** exact creator page, free tier, license and stated clip inventory checked. Native archive, transparent pixels, pivots, scale and runtime behavior remain to be proved after go. - **Design reference:** composition, pacing, hierarchy or motion to study. Its characters, levels, UI artwork, music and branding are not implicitly licensed assets for dex.place. - **Project evidence:** the supplied scale images, existing selected CC0 player, actual current render/capture and Dex's criticism. This is the acceptance anchor; popularity of an external reference never overrides it. Every source chosen after go gets an intake record: exact URL and creator, observed date, pinned revision/archive hash, license text, code/media scope, intended use, changes made, attribution, native-preview verdict and in-scene verdict. Keep original and adapted files separate. A free-looking page or a successful download is not an acceptance result. ## 2. Primary design reference bank The source pages were read during this research. The game/talk descriptions below do not claim fresh complete playthroughs, listening sessions or full video review. User-supplied images in section3 were actually opened and visually inspected. Clip/screenshot review still belongs in the after-go comparison pass. | ID / source | What the source establishes | Proposed lesson for dex.place | Boundary | |---|---|---|---| | REF-01 [Hollow Knight: Forgotten Crossroads, Team Cherry](https://www.teamcherry.com.au/blog/the-forgotten-crossroads-a-hollow-knight-tour) | Creator describes open interconnected tunnels, shortcuts, dangers and occasional friendly travelers | Draw and traverse a real room graph; services interrupt long quiet stretches; return shortcuts make exploration change the route | No copied Hallownest geometry, insect characters, dialogue, hand-drawn art or collectible gates | | REF-02 [Introducing Hollow Knight, Team Cherry](https://www.teamcherry.com.au/blog/introducing-hollow-knight) | Creator describes traditional2D animation, a restrained early visual palette, varied places and inhabitants continuing their tasks | Strong silhouette, limited scene accents, small work gestures, readable enemy states | Early-development description is historical, not a universal recipe for the final game's rendering or a license | | REF-03 [Journey, thatgamecompany](https://thatgamecompany.com/journey/) | Official premise combines a vast landscape, distant destination and chance encounters with companions | Make scale legible through ordinary human-sized cues; let a remote traveler become meaningful against emptiness; create a landmark to move toward | Our game stays side-view pixel art and independent progression, with the explicitly requested voice option | | REF-04 [Eastward, Pixpil/Chucklefish](https://eastwardgame.com/) | Official page presents varied towns/camps/forests, a cast and a detailed material-themed promotional website | Cozy interiors can be warm, useful and furnished; repeated material/typography rules can connect a game to its website | Avoid dense-town population, cooking/quests/gacha, sales slogans and top-down perspective. These are not new features | | REF-05 [Hyper Light Drifter, Heart Machine](https://www.heartmachine.com/) | Developer identifies the game and its ruined-world direction | Secondary study target for color masses, restrained luminous accents and small actors against large ruins | Palette/cluster reference only; no top-down layout, copied characters, music, blood or default neon saturation. Actual shot comparison remains pending | | REF-06 [Bruno Simon's portfolio](https://bruno-simon.com/) and [Folio2025 source](https://github.com/brunosimon/folio-2025) | The site publishes controls/quality/respawn surfaces and links its MIT client source; server code is explicitly withheld | Play can lead naturally to useful content; inspect ordering of input, physics, view, interactions, visuals and audio rather than allowing unrelated handlers to compete | No Three.js/Rapier/car rewrite or imported biography/achievements/whispers. The repo does not supply our presence/voice backend | | REF-07 [Celeste & TowerFall Physics, Maddy Makes Games](https://www.maddymakesgames.com/articles/celeste_and_towerfall_physics/index.html) | Author explains actors/solids, fractional movement remainders and moving-solid carry/push behavior | Use as a diagnostic model for platform edges, stairs and lifts: stable feet, explicit riding, correct pushing and deterministic recovery | Reason about our existing Phaser implementation; no unlicensed engine/code transplant or wholesale physics rewrite by analogy | | REF-08 [Forgiveness Mechanics, Seth Coster / GDC2020](https://www.gdcvault.com/play/1026606/Forgiveness-Mechanics-Reading-Minds-for/) | Speaker's session describes input-tolerance techniques for responsive play | Preserve input buffering and coyote behavior where they express intent, while keeping damage and visible collision trustworthy | Talk listing/abstract reviewed, not a claimed watched recording; no borrowed magic frame counts or new assist features inferred | | REF-09 [The12 principles of animation in video games, Jonathan Cooper](https://www.gamedeveloper.com/production/the-12-principles-of-animation-in-video-games) | Author discusses adapting anticipation, follow-through and other animation principles to game responsiveness | Separate readable anticipation/contact/recovery; allow secondary cable/paper motion after contact without prematurely removing the sword pose | Use concepts and authored donor clips, not copied book prose or one universal easing/animation speed | | REF-10 [Designing Celeste, Maddy Thorson / GDC2017](https://www.gdcvault.com/play/1024307/Level-Design-Workshop-Designing-Celeste) | Official talk catalogue identifies room/stage layout, area-map arrangement and story integration | Study how a complete route is arranged and revised, alongside individual rooms | Catalogue/abstract checked; full talk review remains pending. Do not import precision-platformer difficulty or story systems | | REF-11 [Machinarium, Amanita Design](https://amanita-design.net/games/machinarium.html) | Creator identifies the environmental robot adventure and official media | Reserve reference for service-object staging and readable physical actions | Page search text available but direct fetch failed during this run; no claim of inspected animation. No puzzle/quest/lore import or asset reuse | These sources have different jobs. Hollow Knight supplies the adjacency/solitude reference, Journey the scale/social reference, Eastward the refuge/material reference, and the animation/physics sources the contact/control reference. Do not average their art styles into a collage. ## 3. Dex's supplied scale references These three supplied images were opened locally again on2026-09-08. Original artist/license has not been established, so keep them as private composition references rather than redistributable source art. The intended lessons below are our visual observations. | Reference | Observed relationship | Translation into a side-view pixel scene | |---|---|---| | Submerged giant and diver (private composition reference (not bundled)) | A tiny nearby human cue; an immense cropped form; successive dark structures disappear into haze | Use an oversized partial structure behind a readable small walkway, with several quieter depth planes. Shape must read before surface texture | | Standing figure and distant upright mass (private composition reference (not bundled)) | Ordinary figure and shoreline establish a stable scale; a clear distant silhouette rises through a broad pale field | A tiny door, rail or traveler establishes scale before a huge vertical shaft/tower. Keep a clean silhouette and broad negative space | | Travelers below an enormous rounded form (private composition reference (not bundled)) | Human figures occupy a narrow ground band while one huge continuous form dominates the view | Allow a room's dominant shape to extend well beyond the camera. Avoid filling its empty surroundings with signs, equal-sized pillars and repeated props | None requires copying a monster, changing the game's camera perspective or making the player unreadably small. Pixel art must express those relationships through silhouettes, value separation, repetition at believable scales and depth, not through photorealistic source textures pasted behind sprites. ## 4. Room-specific look and rhythm This table refines21's proposed graph. Palette/light/decoration choices are starting art direction and remain tunable. The functional connections and exact content boundaries stay firm. | Place | Dominant composition | Materials/light/movement | What to avoid | |---|---|---|---| | Arrival | Long quiet ground band, small traveler, one enormous cropped/distant landmark | Cool stone/metal, pale distance, a small restrained warm/red cue, slow distant movement | An opening full of controls, NPCs, particles and evenly spaced decorative pillars | | Junction | Two visibly different route opportunities plus the arena's strongest sightline | Map hangs on a believable fixture; warm refuge doorway and upper route carry different silhouettes | A diagram that promises branches but routes everyone along one corridor | | Hearth/counter | Compression after exposed travel; a protected human-sized pool of warmth | Wood/paper/aged metal, warm local lamp, one attendant and a few coordinated service gestures | A crowded tavern, repeated sales reminders or a white generic account card hovering over unrelated art | | Treasury | A taller ordered interior with a ledger focal point and quiet perimeter | Related paper/metal language, deliberate illumination at the ledger, sparse donation box | Fake prosperity through invented names/counts, coins everywhere, reward-tier spectacle | | Lookout | Open sky/water and a distant route/figure reveal | Wind-led small motion, reduced foreground detail, clean silhouette | Constant combat or fog so thick the next landing disappears | | Reservoir | A distinct enormous volume, successive depth planes, a small useful crossing | Cool muted water/stone, separated haze, a few independent hanging/structural elements | Enlarging a small sprite until its pixels become boulders; a repeating train of platform modules | | Gallery | Quiet arrival, generous space per work, a discernible beginning and return route | Neutral frames and light around the display; art itself stays ungraded/unpixelated | Personal illustrations in global fog/UI textures; opening the entire catalog when inspecting one piece | | Archive | Door threshold reveals unexpected depth; layered shelving gives a sense of interior extent | Paper/cabinets, constrained light shafts, quiet service motion, clear reading surface | A locked-content puzzle, unreadable dark body text or paragraphs trapped in a tiny game popup | | Dispatch/arena | Product identity at the threshold; clear duel ground against a low-noise backdrop | Boss silhouette/telegraph first, contact/impact second, atmosphere third | Busy enemy particles hiding attacks; generic monster pack collage; success overlays before the death beat | Population is part of composition. Service pockets may contain one recognizable worker, while several intervening views contain none. A remote ghost may pass through that silence; do not manufacture a crowd to prove the feature exists. Room-specific enemy caps and spawn intervals are tuned in an actual walking/listening journey. ## 5. Production rules and visible rejection criteria These are project design rules derived from Dex's constraints and the reference roles above. They are not claims that an external source mandates these exact implementation choices. | Rule | Working instruction | Reject the result when | |---|---|---| | DR-01 Scale before detail | Compose the real player, ground band, dominant mass and route in a small thumbnail before decoration | Removing texture makes the scene read as a flat row of props rather than a large place | | DR-02 Connected geography | Give rooms distinct entrances/exits, vertical choices and useful return connections; walk the whole loop early | Branches exist only in the map graphic or every destination is reached by continuing right | | DR-03 Contrast creates scale | Place a sheltered, ordinary room before or after a large reveal; use a known-size door/rail/person | Every space has the same camera distance, vertical extent and prop density | | DR-04 One foreground grid | Compare hero, terminal, floor, doorway and new actors at final play size; record source crop and effective pixel pitch | Assets look like different games or shimmer/chunk differently as the camera moves | | DR-05 Distance has a role | Distant forms may use finer detail/pixels but quieter contrast; keep middle planes distinct | A background competes with the hero or the foreground looks pasted onto a photograph | | DR-06 Flat usable structure | Author side-view floors, frames, supports and openings; keep collision and visible top edges registered | Platform perspective suggests a3D camera that never moves, joints form Lego seams, or the feet float | | DR-07 Material light | Give lights a source and a local effect on world surfaces; keep haze planes separate and restrained | Glow is an arbitrary halo, fog hides interaction/landings, or the entire scene receives one flattening tint | | DR-08 Sparse meaningful motion | Use one or two readable local motions amid slower distant movement; desynchronize natural idles | Every prop pulses on the same loop or particles become the main subject everywhere | | DR-09 Physical contact | Bind action consequences to the actual hit/use event, then let follow-through and secondary parts settle | The sword vanishes before the cut, the wrong cable breaks, or the menu is the only evidence of contact | | DR-10 Readable combat | Distinguish anticipation, active hit and recovery in pose/timing; authored collision windows follow the clip | Damage happens before a readable tell, the hit shape disagrees with the weapon, or effects hide the boss | | DR-11 Reliable movement | Preserve responsive double jump/input tolerance; test stairs, edge landings, moving carry and knockback together | The player sticks on small risers, footsteps machine-gun, or a lift slowly separates from the feet | | DR-12 Discoverable objects | Use placement, silhouette, proximity response and restrained contextual cues; keep full accessible names | Removing large labels makes objects impossible to distinguish, or all scenery falsely looks usable | | DR-13 UI shares materials | Use a small family of frame, backing, edge, shadow and typography parts with real DOM text | Every interface is the same plain card, or every room has a different unrelated UI theme | | DR-14 Reading has room | Use appropriate full web layouts and inner article scrolling; retain ordinary direct URLs | Long text is squeezed into gameplay framing or wheel/touch gestures unexpectedly change modes | | DR-15 Bars serve composition | Tune bars per viewport without hiding feet, attacks or controls; release them naturally into web browsing | Bars simply reduce an already cramped viewport or become a mandatory slow scroll animation | | DR-16 Entry transfers control | One deliberate Enter attempts chosen audio and acquires gameplay; reveal and controls share a known ready state | A second click is needed, the scene looks ready but ignores movement, or music starts as a sudden wall | | DR-17 Typography stays readable | Pixel fonts carry short headings/labels; readable body/fallback fonts handle articles, names, Vietnamese and money | Small glyphs blur, long passages fatigue, names become missing-glyph boxes or QR/bank facts are stylized beyond recognition | | DR-18 Ghosts feel present | Restrained tint, compatible world placement, real activity expiry and identifiable admitted speakers | Ghosts walk over local gaps, appear as opaque crowds, or inactive/blocked/incompatible people remain audible; ordinary camera-edge culling follows22's separate proximity rule | | DR-19 Keep the musical identity | Retain selected SunoB; give arrival breath, coherent calm travel, purposeful arena contrast and reading quiet | New rooms switch to unrelated tracks or material sounds interrupt the emotional pacing | | DR-20 Content remains factual | Let composition carry personality; register concise controls/status rather than importing donor-site copy | A template adds a role tagline, marketing pitch, invented lore or fake popularity to fill space | For pixel comparison, record approximate source cluster size, cropped source bounds, drawn world size and the complete camera/canvas-to-CSS scale. Compare the resulting visible cluster size against the selected hero and adjacent material at normal play size. Do not rely on PNG dimensions or `image-rendering: pixelated` alone. Render snapping and texture sampling should be evaluated separately from physics precision; no blanket physics rewrite is justified by this rule. Rules guide inspection, not asset-count padding or a rigid pixel-coordinate recipe. If a frame meets numbers but looks weak, change it and record why. If a proposal conflicts with a functional requirement, resolve the contract rather than ignoring it in code. ## 6. Motion and assembly recipes to prove after go These are proposed animation anatomies, not generated sprite-sheet requests or claims that a donor already contains the required gesture. Fine timing is tuned using real clips and contact frames. REF-09 motivates the separation of anticipation/contact/follow-through; the actual components and event ownership below are our implementation design. | Assembly | Independent parts | Intent → consequence → settled state | |---|---|---| | Cut map | Fixed support, fastening, attached cable segment, loose cable end, map body, bottom weight, shadow | Sword enters its active window → fastening severs at contact → loose cable drops and body unrolls under its weight → sword completes recovery while paper/weight settle → E inspection becomes available. Close leaves the cut open | | Interior door | Frame, leaf/shutter, handle/indicator, interior darkness/light, threshold transition | Context use moves the door/indicator → doorway reveals a readable transition → target scene is ready → place the traveler at its authored entrance. Failure keeps a safe source-side state | | Lift | Fixed guides/frame, platform, attached moving shoes, restrained wheels/cables, stop indicator | Summon changes local signal → platform travels on guides → exact carry/contact maintained → platform settles at a real floor height. Decorative belts cannot imply an unattached mechanism | | Counter service | Actor idle/approved work clip, counter, independent record/book or service prop, UI backing | Approach gets a small orientation/gesture response → E chooses the service → the themed account/ledger surface opens with real focus. No invented dialogue or fake receipt | | Boss | Authored body clips, separate intentional attack VFX, hit regions, death pieces/state, transition layer | Pose announces action → active contact window → recover; on actual defeat finish death beat → controlled black → correct product menu. No file is requested by the death event | | Art inspector | Physical frame/backing/light, exact DOM image, separate UI frame/caption/controls | E binds one art ID → dedicated inspection emphasizes that work → close returns to the same bay. The collection folder is a separate catalog action | | Scroll handoff | World viewport, independently sized bars, web layout, focus/input/audio owners | Native scroll signals departure → release gameplay/PTT and pause → bars open and full website enters view → ordinary content scrolling. Return restores position with deliberate Resume | Keep animation events in the object's state owner, with idempotent contact and cancellation. A late callback cannot re-open a dismissed menu or reapply a cut. UI presentation timing does not get to corrupt combat completion; gameplay pause does not freeze a half-open DOM surface. Reduced motion preserves the same final physical/semantic result using a shorter transition. ## 7. Interface rules with authoritative behavior references The decorative surface may look like paper, a hanging map, a ledger or a product record. Its controls remain semantic HTML with real labels, focus and data. Use the existing accessible primitives and scoped23 references rather than reproducing semantics inside a canvas. - [W3C modal dialog pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/): use appropriate initial focus, bounded modal focus, a real close action and sensible focus return. Nearby/person popovers follow22's lightweight rules instead of falsely making the whole world modal. - [W3C focus not obscured](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum.html): bars, sticky navigation, paper edges and scroll containers must not cover the focused control. Inspect at real browser zoom, not only enlarged CSS. - [W3C target size minimum](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/target-size-minimum.html): the criterion uses24×24 CSS pixels with defined exceptions. Our proposed comfortable touch-control footprint is larger, around44–48 CSS pixels where space permits; do not mislabel44 as that criterion's minimum. - [W3C contrast minimum](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html): normal text generally needs4.5:1 and large text3:1 under the criterion. Measure actual text over its rendered material, not a flat palette swatch behind a translucent texture. Pixel-font selection in24 is conditional on real glyph coverage and license. Keep Daniel for `dex`, choose one short-label pixel family after comparison, and keep a readable text family/fallback for long documents and account names. Test the actual strings `Downloads`, `dex account`, `THIEU GIA MINH`, `100,000 VND`, a Vietnamese name with accents, an error message and a long article. No font choice is accepted because its specimen alone looks good. ## 8. Short production comparison plan After go, acquire the exact selected code/art sources and retain licenses/hashes. Then make small labeled comparisons inside the actual game and DOM stack: 1. **Actor strip at play size:** current hero beside the strongest boss, mob and townsfolk candidates; idle, locomotion, attack/hit/death or service clip as supplied. Check native silhouette/pivots, feet, outline and pixel pitch. Reject incompatible bodies before scene expansion. 2. **Material junction:** real floor segment/corner, doorframe, map fixture, actor and one background mass. Compare native-pixel and any authorized controlled post-pixelation source at equal world size. Never pixelate UI, artwork or QR. 3. **Two contrasting rooms:** the hearth and the reservoir, connected through a working transition. Check that they feel like one world with different scale/temperature, including Low and narrow-screen versions. 4. **One complete physical action:** sword contact, map cable drop, settling, E map inspection and close. Judge the whole sequence at normal speed and frame-stepped contact; no standalone GIF-only sign-off. 5. **One game-to-web route:** entry sound/focus, boss death/black/product menu, explicit file download, scroll and return. Include keyboard/touch and text zoom early, not after the artwork is frozen. 6. **Social resting place:** two actual clients share an otherwise quiet room, with nearby voice and activity expiry. Judge whether the visitor encounter adds atmosphere without creating constant HUD noise. These comparisons inform the full21/22 implementation. They do not replace completing every room, registered control and real service. Capture accepted and rejected alternatives with a short reason, actual revision and next correction; do not create an endless mood-board phase after go. ## 9. Sound-material sources alongside the selected music Keep selected SunoB and the source/rights/export records in12 and the private audio production root. A new donor pack is raw material for an identified weak effect, not a reason to replace the musical identity. These official pages were checked; no new audio was downloaded or auditioned in this research. | Source | Verified page facts / existing project evidence | Proposed use and actual next proof | |---|---|---| | [Kenney Impact Sounds](https://kenney.nl/assets/impact-sounds) |130 files, free, CC0. The current project's `audio/foley-candidates/PROPOSAL.md` and `audio/recorded-steps-v1/README.md` already document its concrete-footstep originals, licence and runtime derivatives | Start with the owned source and compare actual step/contact timing. Fix cadence, attachment and mix before assuming another sample pack solves weak footsteps. Inspect/replace only the identified material mismatch | | [Kenney Interface Sounds](https://kenney.nl/assets/interface-sounds) |100 files, free, CC0 | Candidate restrained click/service/confirmation texture. Do not attach a generic beep to every action or use UI sound as substitute for a cable/door physically moving. Archive and listening review still pending | | [Kenney RPG Audio](https://kenney.nl/assets/rpg-audio) |50 files, free, CC0; official tags include foley, footsteps and weapons | Reserve physical contact/weapon comparison. Exact clip names, recording quality and fit are unverified until intake/listening; the label RPG does not imply cinematic suitability | SFX timing is bound to meaningful contact/settlement states, with stable material gain and a listening pass under the actual theme/voice mix. Preserve variation that sounds natural; avoid uncontrolled pitch/gain randomization or a footstep on every collision tick. Quiet rooms should have fewer and softer events, not merely a quieter copy of the arena mix. New capture/generation or provider spend remains after-go work with the existing budget boundary. ## 10. Source and review status - Current project sources and the three supplied scale images were read/inspected. Original game reference pages, creator articles, official talk descriptions and W3C pages were checked; a description alone is not a watched video or played scene. - Creator preview observations and exact candidate licenses/free tiers are in24; archive completeness and runtime animation fit remain unverified until intake. - Code licenses and installed/upstream version differences are in23. A source example is not a verified installed integration or a reason to upgrade the whole stack. - Current SunoB/source provenance and authored Martial Hero remain the selected local materials. No new soundtrack, provider generation, repo clone, package install, asset acquisition or website implementation was performed by this reference-writing turn. - Some source fetches failed or returned only a small image/link. Those are explicitly marked; do not treat a resolved image URL as proof that its animation was inspected. No remote media was downloaded to work around a preview limitation. - Any public documentation release must include23–25 through an updated allowlist/privacy transform. Private local reference paths and unlicensed reference imagery must not be copied into the public ZIP. Published edition1.0 remains immutable; the next go owns the new public edition.

title: Version 2 implementation record
bodyMarkdown: # Version 2 implementation record Public documentation edition1.1, source specification2.1. The inhabited second version is in active implementation. This chapter records the actual checkpoint; it does not convert planned features or isolated tests into public-release acceptance. Earlier planning holds in21–25 are historical and superseded by this implementation record. ## Kickoff and ownership The active candidate entry is `src/worldsite/v2/main.tsx`; the first-pass entry remains as history. Existing public hosting and its retained rollback remain authoritative until a verified promotion. Published documentation1.0 is immutable; later reader/ZIP changes use this separate edition. Source, runtime assets, account services, preview plates and documentation must refer to the same reviewed revision. Detailed workstation, account-provider and operator records stay private. ## Current evidence state V2-01–V2-24 and N22-01–N22-16 started untested for the new candidate. The scoped local, native-App and managed-media evidence below now covers parts of that matrix; the complete pass is not accepted. First-pass public/browser/media receipts retain only their original scope. Record exact code/source/asset changes and visible/listening proofs here or in linked bounded receipts; never convert a source example, generated reference or fixture into broader acceptance. ## Execution sequence Preserve baseline → prove account/voice feasibility and establish stable interfaces → traverse complete nonlinear map → build the connected intro/cut/door/mob/boss/product/web route → finish layered rooms/UI/actors/audio and actual services → repeated taste inspection and replacement → full device/accessibility/multi-client/public verification → new documentation edition and reviewed public promotion. Actual payment/purchase, identity/security and destructive unknown-data gates remain action-specific. Continue independent work if one external fact needs the user; do not replace required services with mocks or silently drop them. ## Implementation checkpoint — local candidate, not public - The candidate has eleven connected spaces, twenty-three directed doors, a permanently released physical map, individual art intents, a counter, treasury, separate archive, a return lift and reservoir crossing. Normal damage, nearby respawn and authored boss death are implemented. Each new world product-menu visit consumes a fresh encounter; direct website downloads remain immediately available. - The active React entry joins the intro, immediate world focus, cinematic bars, native scrolling website, material panels, account services, and lightweight nearby/voice controls. Integration and visual inspection remain in progress. A successful module test does not accept the complete page. - Selected free-use assets retain original frames and licences: the existing hero, seven additional actor definitions, shared sourced fire, two UI frames, and the selected pixel label font. Eight separately generated world pieces now cover counter, archive surround/leaf, fireplace, caretaker wall, canopy, bookcase and distant hollow stone; a separate generated paper material serves the DOM. [19](world-asset-inventory.md) records the60-role/104-placement snapshot and exact counting boundaries. The warm-room revision responds to a real bare-room taste failure and remains under composed review. No personal illustrations were used as environment materials. - Complete approved Suno arrangement B is byte-preserved. A complete original chamber arena variant, gentler entry and voice ducking are implemented. Browser/audio-budget checks pass; listening in the assembled experience remains required. - The same-origin service adapter has opaque website sessions, account-scoped progress, explicit guest import, verified contribution records and bounded ghost presence. Isolated service/identity fixtures prove local logic, not actual shared registration or email delivery. - Shared account policy and email configuration remain behind the identity service. Confirmation/recovery readiness stays disabled until actual delivery and completion proof; no separate website identity database or changed desktop capability is implied. - The earlier patched local SFU proof remains10/10 at its recorded scope. The selected managed Cloud forwarding path passes seven checks; that same nine-check receipt also retains a passing client-denial check and a failed native-admin-audio comparison. The website HTTP/presence/voice adapter with real Cloud synthetic media has10/10. Auth identities were isolated fixtures, and both clients ran on one machine; no real microphone, physical Samsung/iPad pair or independent-network acceptance follows. The verified route uses per-listener forwarding; the rejected native assumption is not relabeled a pass. No public v2 promotion is implied. - The existing public rollback remains unchanged, with verified private source backups. Private evidence remains outside this edition. Published1.0 reader and archive bytes stay unchanged. ## Current scoped proof ledger These are implementation observations at the linked source hashes, not a completed V2/N22 matrix. Later material, streaming, UI, service or source changes require the relevant final regression. Historical failures remain alongside their corrections. | Evidence | What actually passed | Limit / remaining proof | |---|---|---| | Integrated App v1 (private asset-authoring root) |18 recorded native UI/keyboard checks: immediate entry/movement, scroll/menu input release, double jump, permanent map/E behavior, free Archive route and counter inspection, product approach and ordinary boss damage/player death with no product menu | The run stopped at a later walking timeout. Earlier checks are scoped evidence, not a clean complete tour | | Integrated App v2 (private asset-authoring root) | Native upper route, ordinary rat/bat defeats, all nine distinct physical artwork displays, return-lift carry and return doors | A broad unavailable-word assertion matched the article's specification prose and failed. The actual reader continuation is verified separately; this original failed receipt remains intact | | Integrated App v3 (private asset-authoring root) | Eight checks after normal reload of the actual prior browser storage: canonical1.1 article and pause, native return to Dispatch, UI-selected8HP encounter, complete assisted boss death into product page with zero automatic downloads, and a fresh fight for another world visit | Boss victory explicitly used the existing assistance control. This is not unassisted balance/victory proof. No game-state/pose/save injection or route fixture was used in this continuation | | Combined actual-App geography | All eleven rooms and nine artwork identities were reached across those native routes | This is combined branch coverage, not one flawless fresh frozen end-to-end run. Recent warm materials and tiny composition refinements postdate those receipts | | Room streaming (private asset-authoring root) |9/9 native App checks: first-room hydration, visible non-gallery door/cut prompts, delayed/failed destination safety, actual Retry passage, pause/resume while loading and reuse of a hydrated room | Two real image requests were deliberately delayed and one aborted; no replacement texture or game-state injection. Full-device performance and final texture budgets remain separate | | Audio (private asset-authoring root) |45 browser/codec checks, five actual-game event-to-audio checks, two stale-selection rejection checks. Complete B unchanged; chamber cue, reader/art silence, combat effects and voice ducking implemented. Peak measured cache/reservation64,806,772bytes below64MiB | Source-rate AudioBuffer proof, not total process memory. New assembled listening, real voice audibility and physical-device behavior still require judgment | | Mounted production origin (private asset-authoring root) | Final17/17 current-hash checks: actual static/API mount, canonical HTTPS-origin host-only Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite cookie headers, CSRF/Origin denial, guest rotation, protected data, API no-store/JSON, static/ranges/gzip/redirects, private-path denial, SP13 fixture rules, trusted-proxy rate separation and idempotent cleanup | Isolated ephemeral loopback origin and data root; logical Host dex.place is reverse-proxy-origin proof, not public TLS/browser acceptance. Voice used an inactive cleanup spy. No real account mutation, email, microphone, public task/origin change or persistent fixture data | | Private owner packet (private asset-authoring root) | Current Node service bundles/imports with pinned SDK licences. Runtime, static server, bootstrap and PowerShell launcher are hash-frozen together outside public output | Actual production config/data/credentials are excluded. Root owns metadata sealing, lifecycle and promotion; configuration existence is not deployment proof | | Documentation1.1 candidate (private asset-authoring root) |28 chapters,318 portable links, preserved control IDs, four actual physical-file destinations and exact30-member reader/ZIP parity. Published1.0 remains29 unchanged files. The generated catalog retains old1.0 readers/archives | Unpublished/unfrozen1.1 must be regenerated after this source reconciliation and final evidence. The prior1.1 ZIP was302191bytes, SHA256 `ab039ff663f194211a89ee5cf1172bd64bbfb5dfc1342db4d02d24b844da27bd`; it is a checkpoint, not the final export identity | Current service detail: the service lane reports15/15 isolated HTTP/store/auth-fixture cases, including refresh concurrency and bounded join reservations. Managed protocol (private production review records) and website-to-Cloud media (private production review records) retain real transport/decoding evidence while explicitly marking synthetic audio and fixture identities. Newer privacy/capacity refinements still need final integrated receipt refresh. Real shared-provider sign-in/registration/confirmation/recovery and actual owner enrollment remain unverified; email readiness is false and no real owner UUID is assigned at this checkpoint. A read-only mounted capability lookup returned providerReady/password true, with signup/Google/recovery/confirmation false. ## UI completion decisions before implementation The Menu's Map action appears only after local `cut.map.junction` is recorded; it reopens the existing non-travel inspection and never cuts or teleports. The physical release remains meaningful, with the existing keyboard/touch/hold-to-attack routes retained. Mobile receives the missing Dash equivalent of Shift. Game-action buttons use a compact two-by-two action group at narrow widths, retain the selected touch size, and leave a separate place for intentional hold-to-talk. The scrolling Illustrations slot retains its measured layout height while its offscreen art component unmounts. This does not retain hidden images or authorize offscreen art requests. Browser Back/Forward between versions of the same currently open victory product preserves that one visit; leaving the product still ends it, and history cannot resurrect an ended visit. Closing a system menu returns to its actual prior context: submenus return to Menu, game-opened Menu closes back to the paused game's input owner, and web-opened controls return focus without jumping into play. Renderer failure after entry clears stale passage presentation and offers explicit world Retry plus website access; it cannot leave a dead Resume button. These are completion/fix decisions within the existing control contracts, with focused native proof still required. Saved-room restoration is part of entry readiness: initial Enter and recovery Resume remain honestly Loading until the target resources are ready. A separate prepared passage phase means resources are hydrated but the opening has not begun; it permits Resume even when loading completed while paused, preventing a readiness deadlock. Closing/browsing away from a physical inspection releases only its originating presentation through the gameplay-owned close-inspection command. Returning to gameplay through the canvas or Resume ends a victory-product visit just as the explicit Return to world action does. ### Focused UI completion proof The UI completion receipts (private asset-authoring root) now record18/18 desktop/true-coarse-pointer checks,13/13 native assisted-victory/history checks,13/13 final route/loading/error checks and one explicit unavailable-product fixture. Each successful run had stable source hashes and no page errors. The final edge run still matches the handed-off UI/game sources; earlier runs retain their specific revision scope. This is focused coverage, not the complete final device/taste/public matrix. The desktop gallery retained its942px measured slot when withdrawn: document height6504px and footer position5366px stayed unchanged, image elements unmounted, and no new art requests started. Portrait390×844 and landscape844×390 native coarse-pointer contexts exercised actual Dash and all six Large touch targets without overlap or clipping; screenshots were inspected. These are browser-emulated contexts, not physical Samsung/iPad proof. The voice pad is separately centered, respects touch size and is absent while a covering HUD is open; real joined-microphone layout/behavior remains a media test. The assisted test used the actual earlier native browser's saved exploration, normal reload, UI settings and ordinary controls. A real8HP authored fight reached the product menu with no automatic download; selecting1.0/1.1 and browser Back/Forward preserved the one active visit, while gameplay return ended it and subsequent history did not resurrect it. It does not prove ordinary unassisted victory balance. Real renderer-loss injection exposed the new Retry world action, removed stale passage/Resume state and recreated a ready world through explicit retry. Saved-room and paused-passage loading gates were verified with one delayed real image request; prepared Resume completed without deadlock. Unknown root/account/donation addresses now show Page unavailable with four primary navigation links and recovery; malformed art/product IDs remain in their respective content errors without hidden art requests. Deep-link/history navigation positions the target immediately. Focused DOM J/Space does not attack/jump. A canceled Sound enable originally restored the icon incorrectly after mute; the callback now reads actual audio state and the reproduction passes. An unavailable product never reports Download requested. A deliberately failed VoicePanel import is caught; because the browser cached the failed module, its ineffective same-document retry was replaced with explicit Reload page, which recovered after removal of the fault. An active arena additionally explains that reloading restarts that fight. No microphone, account, payment, clipboard or public action was used in these UI checks. ## Final candidate integration checkpoint The real primary dex account now passes website login/reload/history/owner-read/logout and an explicit import of ordinary-input guest exploration (8/8). A fresh delivered recovery email returns to its originating website cookie/PKCE flow and the empty new-password form (4/4); the preserved primary credential was not changed. Existing-account signup keeps its generic verification-required behavior and original login (3/3). Isolated new-user/cancel cases remain separately labelled (8/8). The shared foundation's native new-user confirmation and password recovery prove the provider primitives. Production readiness is prepared from these facts; actual public-origin verification remains after promotion. Ko-fi's existing account exposes free webhook configuration. The website now has authenticated, bounded, idempotent notification intake and private owner review. Tests and conflicts are quarantined, and notifications never automatically confirm money, link accounts or publish names/amounts. Ordinary records require separate trusted evidence and the existing manual confirmation flow. Protocol and owner UI each passed7 checks; full current service tests pass24. Its protected verification ref has been enrolled; public endpoint/provider test activation waits the candidate origin. No payment occurred and the public treasury remains empty. The material pass now defines60 world roles and116 placements, with all11 rooms rendered and inspected. Hearth has separately generated wall/timber/bookcase/fireplace pieces and original animated fire; the lookout landmark is grounded behind the water; archive shelving, aspect-correct gallery frames/windows and uncluttered arena architecture replace the earlier bare/placeholder compositions. Current visual pass (private asset-authoring root) records the exact scope. Personal artwork remains restricted to active DOM illustration display. Loading previews use35 actual renderer captures: five destinations at compact landscape, phone portrait, tablet portrait, tablet landscape, desktop16:10, desktop16:9 and ultrawide. Their anchors, room bounds, map/scene/room and every source image hash are recorded. The initial preview is mounted; the exact desktop frame fixes a visibly shifting parallax handoff. First-impression checks confirmed immediate control and no clipping/art requests on five browser profiles. Secondary text contrast and an opaque sticky navigation backing were corrected; metadata-only gallery reservation prevents direct documentation links from shifting or loading unrelated personal art. The audio manager now limits audible-speech music ducking to6dB and lets a just-started physical inspection cue end within180ms before reader/art silence. Immediate mute/blur/disposal still stop it.23 native checks verify timing, cancellation, final gains and the64MiB AudioBuffer budget; the selected21 entries and25 media representations retain their identities. Complete user-selected SunoB is unchanged. The new chamber arena variant remains subject to actual listening; a model without audio input cannot claim to have heard it. ## Concrete remaining acceptance work - **V2-01/02/04/18/20 — final assembled taste and complete UI:** inspect the newly furnished Hearth/Archive, monumental exteriors, pixel pitch, door/map/prop states, silhouettes, modest typography, empty/long/error menus and mobile compositions. The earlier bare warm rooms failed taste. New material count or a working sprite does not close that failure. - **V2-03/05/06/07/09/10/11/12 — frozen gameplay-to-site journey:** repeat current entry/focus/scroll and input-cancellation boundaries on the settled source; include new streaming Retry/cancel, permanent-map reload, normal damage/recovery, ordinary boss readability/balance, death-to-black-to-menu, deliberate actual artifact download and fresh subsequent visit. Preserve the distinction between assisted success, unassisted defeat and an unassisted victory test. - **V2-13 and N22-01–05/15 — real shared identity:** prove the existing account subject across products, live signup/confirmation/recovery/callback lifecycle, account switching/logout, explicit guest merge and accessible account flows. Isolated identities and capability flags do not satisfy this. The shared foundation owns SMTP/auth policy; do not duplicate it or enable readiness without actual delivery/completion proof. - **V2-14 and N22-06–08 — actual owner/treasury operation:** enroll/verify the real owner role and finish the evidenced confirmation/correction workflow, with privacy/deduplication and truthful empty production state. No test donation is required. Regress the existing Ko-fi/MB recipient/amount/QR behavior inside the rebuilt page; retain the prior real bank recipient/100k confirmation without inventing a separately proven image-import method. - **V2-15–17 and N22-09–14 — final social/media integration:** real independent clients, private-world compatibility,60-second movement-or-talk activity, pause/full-content withdrawal, mute/block and permission/cancel/blur/reconnect cases. Complete real-microphone and separate-network Samsung/iPad media checks, with capacity/egress/plan evidence. Managed synthetic one-machine forwarding is useful but narrower. - **V2-19/21/22 — listening, performance and access:** hear the complete calm travel/arena/quiet/SFX/voice mix; measure current cold load, room streaming, frame time and image/audio memory under the final expanded asset set. Verify Low/reduced motion and requested physical browsers, desktop compatibility, true200% zoom, keyboard and actual screen-reader speech on the v2 page. First-pass device reports and AX snapshots do not establish these new results. - **V2-23/24 and N22-16 — final export/stage/promotion:** refresh source-scoped reader1.1 and ZIP, current scene/map/room-matched loading previews, release asset counts/closure and frozen origin/service files. Complete staged HTTP/App/privacy/licence proof, then exact public TLS/routes/downloads/callback/media checks with rollback. Public H and frozen1.0 remain the live baseline until that promotion succeeds. This list preserves all agreed work. A genuine external gate pauses its dependent action, while independent implementation and taste refinement continue. It is not authorization to replace missing services with mocks or to mark the full goal complete from proof counts.
